title: When the Patient Cannot See the Form

patient.name: Mr Mohamed Azri bin Hamid
patient.presenting_complaint: Worsening vision — referred from polyclinic for specialist review

history.hpc: Mr Azri is a 72-year-old with advanced age-related macular degeneration in both eyes, referred for assessment of worsening central vision. He cannot read the SNEC patient registration form — he cannot see even the large print fields clearly. He is accompanied by his grandson, Haziq (aged 19), who offers to fill in the forms for him. Mr Azri is cognitively intact and can answer questions verbally. He does not have hearing difficulties.
history.pmhx: Age-related macular degeneration (AMD) — bilateral, advanced. Hypertension. Type 2 diabetes mellitus (well-controlled). Prostate enlargement on tamsulosin.
history.family_hx: Not known — patient says 'I cannot remember'
history.social_hx: Widower. Lives with grandson Haziq. Grandson is the main caregiver. Mr Azri can still walk independently but uses a white cane outdoors.

examination_findings.fundus: Not assessed at this stage — doctor to review

investigations.va_distance: Tested at closest distance — unable to read LogMAR chart. RE: HM at 50cm. LE: CF at 1m.

diagnosis: History successfully obtained verbally for a patient with severe visual impairment. VA recorded using standard low-vision notation. Grandson's assistance used only for confirmation — primary history taken from patient himself.

immediate: Introduce yourself clearly: give your name, your role as PSA, and where you are in the clinic so the patient can orient himself
Confirm the patient's identity verbally: ask for his full name and NRIC number — he can state this even if he cannot see
Explain that you will read the form to him and fill it in based on his verbal answers
Speak directly to the patient — not to the grandson — unless the patient asks Haziq to help with a specific item
Grandson may help with names of medications if patient cannot recall exactly — but clinical history must come from the patient
Ask one question at a time clearly and give him time to answer — he is cognitively intact
Read back each completed section to the patient for confirmation before moving on
Obtain verbal consent for the history form in lieu of written signature — document 'unable to sign due to visual impairment, verbal consent given' and your own name as witness
Assist patient to the VA testing area and explain the modified test: 'I will ask you to tell me when you can see my hand move or count my fingers — there is no chart needed'
follow_up: Hand completed form to the nurse with a note that verbal consent was obtained
Ensure patient knows the waiting area and that someone will come to escort him when it is his turn
Inform nurse or doctor of the patient's mobility needs (white cane user)
patient_education: Reassure patient that staff are aware he cannot see the forms and will assist him throughout
Inform Haziq about the clinic process so he can support his grandfather appropriately
Do not make assumptions about cognitive ability based on visual impairment

key_points: Verifies identity verbally — does not rely on the patient reading a form
Speaks directly to the patient first, not the accompanying family member
Takes full history verbally and documents it accurately on the form
Allows grandson to assist only with factual items the patient cannot recall (e.g., medication names)
Adapts VA testing to the patient's visual level — uses HM or CF method instead of chart
Obtains VA for both eyes using appropriate notation (HM, CF, PL, NPL)
Explains the modified test to the patient clearly before starting
Documents results accurately using correct clinical abbreviations
Recognises the patient is cognitively intact — does not over-involve the family member inappropriately
Correctly substitutes verbal consent and documents the reason (visual impairment, unable to sign)
Identifies the need to adapt all interactions — seating, guiding, explaining verbally
Does not delay or skip history because of the visual impairment
Guides and positions the patient safely throughout the interaction
Obtains and documents verbal consent with own name as witness
Completes the full history form verbally and reads it back for confirmation
Communicates patient's mobility needs to clinical staff
